definition_en: a woman who is an ambassador, or historically the wife of an ambassador
core_image: 使馆门口，一位女士代表国家迎接宾客
scene: 使馆晚宴前，一位女外交官站在门口迎接客人。 The ambassadress greeted the guests at the embassy door.
sceneCN: 这里 ambassadress 是「女大使」（第 1 个义项：担任大使职务的女性）；句意为这位女大使在使馆门口迎接客人。

pos.zh: 名词：女大使；女大使夫人

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「大使」，ambassadress 由它加阴性后缀构成
由 ambassador 加 -ial 构成，义为「大使的；大使级的」
同源名词，义为「大使馆；大使馆全体人员」

senses.title: A woman serving as ambassador
senses.definition: a woman who holds the official rank of ambassador and represents her country abroad
senses.definitionCN: 担任大使正式职衔、在国外代表本国的女性
senses.example: The ambassadress presented her credentials at the palace.
senses.exampleCN: 这位女大使在宫殿递交了国书。
senses.why: The -ess suffix once marked a woman holding the same office; ambassadress is simply ambassador with that old feminine ending.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ess 曾标记担任同一职务的女性；ambassadress 就是 ambassador 加上这个古老的阴性词尾。

senses.title: The wife of an ambassador
senses.definition: a historical use for the wife of an ambassador, especially when she had a formal social role
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指大使的妻子，尤其当她承担正式社交职责时
senses.example: In the old photographs, the ambassadress stands beside the ambassador.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧照片里，大使夫人站在大使身旁。
senses.why: When diplomatic life assigned a public role to the ambassador's wife, the feminine form named that role rather than the office.
senses.whyCN: 当外交生活给大使的妻子分配了公开角色时，这个阴性形式命名的就是那个角色，而不是官职。

intro.en: Ambassadress is ambassador plus an old feminine ending, and the word carries the history of diplomatic titles.
intro.cn: ambassadress 是 ambassador 加上古老的阴性词尾，这个词带着外交头衔的历史。

items.en: Ambactus meant 'servant, retainer', a word borrowed into Latin from a Celtic source.
items.cn: ambactus 意为「仆人、随从」，是拉丁语从凯尔特语借入的词。

items.en: Old French ambassadeur named an envoy sent on a mission.
items.cn: 古法语 ambassadeur 指被派去执行使命的使节。

items.en: English ambassador entered in the fourteenth century as the title of a senior envoy.
items.cn: 英语 ambassador 于十四世纪进入，指高级使节的头衔。

items.en: The French feminine suffix -esse was added to make ambassadress, first for the wife and later for a woman in the office.
items.cn: 加上法语阴性后缀 -esse 构成 ambassadress，最初指大使夫人，后来也指担任该职务的女性。

items.en: The form is recorded in English from the eighteenth century and was common in formal writing.
items.cn: 这个形式自十八世纪在英语中有记录，并在正式书面语中常见。

items.en: Today many writers prefer ambassador for both sexes, and ambassadress sounds old or ceremonial.
items.cn: 今天许多作者对两性都用 ambassador，ambassadress 听起来古老或带仪式感。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the diplomatic family; the near-meaning group gathers envoys and diplomats.
note.cn: 形近组收外交词族；近义组收使节与外交官。

entries.definition: The base title for a senior envoy.
entries.definitionCN: 指高级使节的基础头衔。

entries.definition: The office or residence of an ambassador.
entries.definitionCN: 指大使的办公处或官邸。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to an ambassador.
A messenger or representative sent on a mission.
entries.definitionCN: 指被派执行使命的使者或代表。

entries.definition: An official who represents a country abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 指在国外代表本国的官员。

entries.definition: A senior diplomat, often below an ambassador in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 指高级外交官，级别通常低于大使。

entries.definition: A person chosen to speak or act for a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指被选出来为团体发言或行事的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the ambassador title and then add the old feminine ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从 ambassador 头衔开始，再加上古老的阴性词尾。

normal.en: Ambassadress is ambassador plus -ess, the old mark of a woman.
normal.cn: ambassadress 就是 ambassador 加上 -ess，这个古老的女性标记。

normal.en: The word first named the ambassador's wife, then a woman holding the office.
normal.cn: 这个词先指大使夫人，后指担任该职务的女性。

normal.en: Embassy is the building; ambassador is the title; ambassadress is the old feminine title.
normal.cn: embassy 是建筑；ambassador 是头衔；ambassadress 是古老的阴性头衔。

normal.en: Modern style often drops the -ess and calls everyone ambassador.
normal.cn: 现代文体常去掉 -ess，对所有人都用 ambassador。

normal.en: Picture the embassy door, with a woman receiving guests in the name of her country.
normal.cn: 想象使馆门口，一位女士以国家的名义迎接宾客。

abstract.en: Picture a formal hall where a title is handed over with sealed papers.
abstract.cn: 想象一座正式大厅，头衔随密封文书一同交接。

abstract.en: Now picture the same hall a century later, the title shared by both sexes.
abstract.cn: 再想象一个世纪后的同一座大厅，头衔由两性共享。

abstract.en: The old -ess is the fossil the word carries from the first hall.
abstract.cn: 古老的 -ess 就是这个词从第一座大厅带来的化石。

examples.en: The ambassadress opened the cultural exhibition.
examples.cn: 这位女大使为文化展开幕。

examples.en: The ambassadress and her husband hosted the reception.
examples.cn: 女大使和她的丈夫主持了招待会。

examples.en: In the old portrait, the ambassadress wears a formal gown.
examples.cn: 在旧画像里，大使夫人穿着正式长裙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺拔丝得瑞斯」——俺拔丝，得瑞斯女士，使馆门口迎客

root: 拉丁语 ambactus（仆人、随从）经古法语 ambassadeur 进入英语作 ambassador；再加法语阴性后缀 -esse 构成 ambassadress，先指大使夫人，后指女大使。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses split between the office and the social role: a woman ambassador, or historically the ambassador's wife.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项分在官职与社交角色之间：担任大使的女性，或历史上的大使夫人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman stands at the embassy door, receiving guests in the name of her country.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位女士站在使馆门口，以国家的名义迎接宾客。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: the first sense is a woman who holds the rank itself.
branches.cn: 官职线：第一个义项是担任该职衔本身的女性。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: the second sense is the ambassador's wife in her public role.
branches.cn: 家庭线：第二个义项是大使的妻子在公开角色中。

branches.en: THE DOOR: both senses meet at the embassy entrance.
branches.cn: 门口线：两个义项都在使馆门口相遇。

branches.en: THE OLD TITLE: the wife sense is the older, ceremonial layer.
branches.cn: 旧头衔线：夫人义是更古老、更仪式化的一层。

branches.en: THE NEW TITLE: the office sense is the modern reading.
branches.cn: 新头衔线：官职义是现代读法。

intro.en: Ambassadress is ambassador with a feminine suffix, and its family is the diplomatic vocabulary around it.
intro.cn: ambassadress 是带阴性后缀的 ambassador，词族是它周围的外交词汇。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ambactus is the distant source of the ambassador family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ambactus 是 ambassador 词族的远源。

items.example: The embassy is near the river.
An envoy was sent to negotiate.

items.meaning: the woman ambassador posted to a country
items.example: She became the ambassadress to France.

items.meaning: a woman who once held the post
items.exampleCN: 这位前女大使现在教书。

definition_en: a large formal meeting of representatives, or the law-making body of some countries
core_image: 圆形大厅里，几百名代表同时举手
scene: 大会主席敲了一下木槌，请各地代表就座。 The congress opened with a long roll call.
sceneCN: 这里 congress 指「代表大会」（第 1 个义项：代表聚集的正式会议）；句意是这场大会以漫长的点名开场。

senses.title: A meeting of delegates
senses.definition: a large formal meeting where delegates discuss shared business
senses.definitionCN: 代表们讨论共同事务的大型正式会议
senses.example: The medical congress drew experts from twenty countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这次医学大会吸引了二十个国家的专家。
senses.why: People who speak for others sit in one room and decide together.
senses.whyCN: 替别人说话的人坐在同一间屋子里，一起决定事情。

senses.title: The law-making body
senses.definition: the national law-making body of some countries, especially the United States
senses.definitionCN: 某些国家的最高立法机构，尤指美国国会
senses.example: Congress passed the bill after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 国会经过长时间辩论通过了这项法案。
senses.why: A meeting that never ends becomes an institution with rules and a building.
senses.whyCN: 一场不会结束的会议，会变成有规章有楼宇的机构。

senses.title: A coming together
senses.definition: the act of coming together, an older and rarer sense
senses.definitionCN: 聚集到一起的行为，是较古老且少用的义项
senses.example: Old maps marked the congress of two rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的地图上标出了两条河流的交汇处。
senses.why: Before it named a hall, the word simply named bodies moving to one point.
senses.whyCN: 在指一座大厅之前，这个词只表示许多身体走向同一点。

intro.en: Congress comes from Latin congressus, a coming together, from com-, together, and gradi, to step or walk.
intro.cn: congress 来自拉丁语 congressus，意为走到一起，由 com-（一起）与 gradi（迈步）构成。

items.en: Gradi meant to step or walk forward.
items.cn: gradi 意为迈步或向前行走。

items.en: Congressus named the act of walking together to one place.
items.cn: congressus 指一起走到同一个地方的行为。

items.en: Old French congres used the word for an assembly of people.
items.cn: 古法语 congres 用这个词指人群的集会。

items.en: English congress first meant a formal meeting of representatives.
items.cn: 英语 congress 最初指代表的正式会议。

items.en: American usage gave it the sense of a national law-making body.
items.cn: 美国用法赋予它国家立法机构的含义。

items.en: It now covers both a single conference and a permanent parliament.
items.cn: 如今它既指一次会议，也指常设的议会。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin step base or the ending of congress, and the meaning group names other law-making bodies.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语迈步词基或 congress 的词尾，近义组列出其他立法机构。

entries.definition: relating to a congress or its members
movement forward toward a better state
a large meeting for discussion
the law-making body of a country such as Britain
the upper house of a law-making body
a group of people gathered for a purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from delegates walking into one hall, then move to debate and to a permanent chamber.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从代表们走进同一座大厅开始，再到辩论，最后到常设的议事厅。

normal.en: Con- is together and gress is step, so congress is people stepping into one room.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，gress 是迈步，congress 就是众人迈步走进同一间屋子。

normal.en: A congress begins as a meeting and can harden into a parliament.
normal.cn: 代表大会起初只是一场会议，也可能固化成议会。

normal.en: Think of a hall where every seat carries a state or a hospital name.
normal.cn: 想象一座大厅，每个座位都写着州名或医院的名字。

normal.en: A conference lasts days, but a congress keeps a building and a budget.
normal.cn: 研讨会只持续几天，而国会拥有固定的楼宇与预算。

normal.en: When delegates stop walking, the debate starts.
normal.cn: 代表们停下脚步的时候，辩论就开始了。

abstract.en: Picture hundreds of name cards on one long table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌上摆着几百个姓名牌。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden hammer falling on a round hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一把木槌落在圆形大厅里。

abstract.en: Picture many roads meeting at one gate.
abstract.cn: 想象许多条路在同一座门前汇合。

examples.en: The congress will meet in the capital next spring.
examples.cn: 大会明年春天将在首都召开。

examples.en: Congress voted against the new tax.
examples.cn: 国会投票否决了新税。

examples.en: She spoke at an international congress on heart disease.
examples.cn: 她在一个国际心脏病大会上发言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 congress 记成 con（一起）加 gress（走）：一群人一起走到同一间屋子里开会，就是代表大会，进而指国会。

root: 源自拉丁语 congressus（com 一起 + gradi 迈步），本义是走到一起，后指代表集会与立法机构。

sensesIntro.en: From bodies walking into one hall, to a formal meeting, and finally to a permanent law-making body.
sensesIntro.cn: 从众人走进同一座大厅，到一场正式会议，最后到常设的立法机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many delegates walking in through one wide door.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多代表从同一扇大门走进来。

branches.en: A congress is first of all a large meeting for shared business.
branches.cn: 代表大会首先是为共同事务召开的大型会议。

branches.en: When the meeting becomes permanent, it turns into a law-making body.
branches.cn: 当会议变成常设机构，它就成了立法机关。

branches.en: The old sense simply names things coming to one point.
branches.cn: 古老义项只表示事物汇聚到同一点。

branches.en: Both senses keep the same picture of a room where voices are counted.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留同一幅画面：一间把声音数清楚的屋子。

branches.en: The national body is the meeting that never goes home.
branches.cn: 国家立法机构就是那场永不散会的会议。

intro.en: Congress is built on Latin com-, together, plus gradi, to step.
intro.cn: congress 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 gradi（迈步）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin step base gress- also appears in progress, regress and aggressive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的迈步词基 gress- 也出现在 progress、regress 与 aggressive 中。

items.meaning: a male member of a congress

items.meaning: a female member of a congress

会谈取得了真正的进展。

items.meaning: to move back to an earlier state
items.exampleCN: 不加练习，技能就会退化。

items.meaning: ready to step forward and attack
items.example: The dog gave an aggressive bark.
items.exampleCN: 那条狗发出攻击性的吠叫。

items.meaning: happening one small step at a time

definition_en: made of parts that are all the same kind
core_image: 一整块颜色均匀的木头，看不出拼接的痕迹
scene: 这个班的学生水平比较整齐。 The class is fairly homogeneous in level.
sceneCN: 这里 homogeneous 是「同质的、成分一致的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个班的学生水平比较整齐。

senses.title: All of one kind
senses.definition: made of parts of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 由同一种类的部分构成
senses.example: The class is fairly homogeneous in level.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班的学生水平比较整齐。
senses.why: This is the core sense of sameness in kind.
senses.whyCN: 这是「种类相同」的核心义项。

senses.title: Evenly mixed
senses.definition: mixed so that the parts are evenly spread
senses.definitionCN: 混合后各部分分布均匀
senses.example: The mixture is homogeneous after stirring.
senses.exampleCN: 搅拌后混合物变得均匀。
senses.why: Here the focus is even distribution.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调的是分布均匀。

intro.en: Homogeneous joins Greek homos, same, with genos, kind.
intro.cn: homogeneous 由希腊语 homos（相同）与 genos（种类）组合而成。

items.en: Homos meant the same.
items.cn: homos 意为相同的。

items.en: Genos meant kind or family.
items.cn: genos 意为种类或族类。

items.en: Homogeneus meant of the same kind.
items.cn: homogeneus 意为同种类的。

items.en: Homogeneous entered scientific English.
items.cn: homogeneous 进入科学英语。

items.en: It spread to society and data.
items.cn: 它又扩展到社会与数据领域。

note.en: Homogeneous is compared with look-alike words and with words for sameness.
note.cn: 把 homogeneous 与形近词以及表示相同的词作比较。

abstract.en: Uniformity is comforting and also a little blind.

definition_en: used to introduce a more exact statement or a list of specific items that explains what has just been said
core_image: 说话人停了一下，把手指点在刚说过的那个笼统词上，补出它确切的名字
scene: 会议散场后，两个同事在走廊里压低声音核对证书上的措辞，其中一人伸手指了指纸上的最后一行。 Only one name can go on the certificate, namely the person who took the course.
sceneCN: 这里是「即、也就是」（第 1 个义项：把前面的话说得更具体）；句意是证书上只能写一个名字，也就是上过这门课的那个人。图中可辨识物件：证书、走廊、手指着的那一行字。

collocations.zh: 即……（后接从句，把前面的话说具体）

derivatives.zh: namely 的基础词，义为「名字」；副词由它加 -ly 构成
由 name 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无名的」
由前缀 re-（重新）与 name 复合而成，义为「重新命名」

senses.title: Introducing a more precise statement
senses.titleCN: 即；也就是（把话说得更具体）
senses.definition: used after a comma to introduce a more exact statement about the thing just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用在逗号之后，引出对刚才所提事物更精确的说法
senses.example: Only one person can sign the contract, namely the owner.
senses.exampleCN: 合同只能由一个人签，也就是业主本人。
senses.why: Namely is name turned into an adverb, so its work is to put the exact name on something the speaker has just left vague.
senses.whyCN: namely 是 name 加后缀变成的副词，它的任务就是给说话人刚说得笼统的东西补上确切的名字。

senses.title: Introducing a list of specific items
senses.titleCN: 即；也就是（列举具体项目）
senses.definition: used after a comma to introduce the particular items that make up a group just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用在逗号之后，引出构成刚才所说整体的具体项目
senses.example: Two countries signed the treaty, namely France and Spain.
senses.exampleCN: 两个国家签署了这项条约，即法国和西班牙。
senses.why: When several names follow one another, the same act of naming becomes an enumeration, which is why the word can introduce a list as well as a single term.
senses.whyCN: 当几个名字接连出现，同一个「点名」的动作就变成了逐项列举，所以这个词既能引出一个名称，也能引出一串项目。

intro.en: Namely is an English adverb built from the noun name, and the adverbial ending that formed it has been in the language since Old English.
intro.cn: namely 是由名词 name 构成的英语副词，构成它的副词词尾自古英语就存在。

items.en: The reconstructed noun for name is the starting point; the adverb is a much later English construction on that base.
items.cn: 起点是重构的表示「名字」的名词；这个副词是在这一基础上很久之后才由英语造出的。

items.en: The reconstructed form namô kept the noun sense of name and passed it into Old English as nama.
items.cn: 重构形式 namô 保留了「名字」的名词义，并以 nama 的形式传入古英语。

items.en: Old English had nama as the noun and the adverb-forming suffix -lice, which could attach to nouns to make adverbs of manner.
items.cn: 古英语有名词 nama，也有构成副词的词尾 -lice，它可以加在名词后构成方式副词。

items.en: Middle English shortened -lice to -li, and name plus -li produced the adverb namely, first used in the sense of by name.
items.cn: 中古英语把 -lice 缩短为 -li，name 加 -li 就造出了副词 namely，最早表示「按名字、指名地」。

items.en: Modern English narrowed the meaning to that is to say, so the word now introduces an exact term or a list rather than naming a person directly.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义收窄为「也就是说」，于是这个词现在引出确切的词语或一串项目，而不再直接给某人点名。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and the words built on the same base; the near-meaning group collects phrases that restate something more exactly.
note.cn: 形近组收那个名词以及建在同一基础上的词；近义组收把前文说得更确切的说法。

entries.definition: The noun from which the adverb is built, meaning the word by which something is known.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个副词的名词，义为「名字」。

entries.definition: Without a name, or too ordinary or bad to be given one.
entries.definitionCN: 没有名字的，或平凡、恶劣得无法命名的。

entries.definition: In name only, or according to what is officially stated; from Latin nomen.
entries.definitionCN: 名义上的，或按官方说法；出自拉丁语 nomen。

entries.definition: To give a new or different name to something.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物取新的或不同的名字。

entries.definition: A phrase used to introduce a clearer version of what was just said.
entries.definitionCN: 用来引出对刚才所说内容的更清楚版本。

entries.definition: A longer phrase with the same job of restating something more exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 一个更长的说法，作用相同，都是把前文更确切地重说一遍。

entries.definition: In a way that names the exact thing rather than a general class.
entries.definitionCN: 点明确切事物而不是笼统类别的说法。

entries.definition: A phrase that repeats an idea in a different and usually simpler form.
entries.definitionCN: 用另一种、通常更简单的说法重复同一个意思。

normalIntro.en: The word is a noun turned adverb, and its one job is to replace a vague phrase with an exact name or a list of names.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是由名词变成的副词，唯一的任务就是用确切的名字或一串名字替换笼统的说法。

normal.en: Namely is name plus -ly, so the adverb literally carries the noun's job of naming.
normal.cn: namely 是 name 加 -ly，所以这个副词本身就带着名词「命名」的职责。

normal.en: The modern -ly comes from Old English -lice, which is why the ending looks like the ending of other manner adverbs.
normal.cn: 现代的 -ly 来自古英语 -lice，所以这个词尾看起来和其他方式副词一样。

normal.en: Namely sits after a comma and before the exact term, and it never begins a sentence on its own.
normal.cn: namely 站在逗号之后、确切词语之前，从不单独起句。

normal.en: Namely introduces a noun phrase or a list rather than a full clause, so a whole sentence after it is usually wrong.
normal.cn: namely 引出的是名词短语或一串项目，而不是完整从句，所以后面接整句通常是错的。

normal.en: The older sense was by name, which shows that the word began as a way of pointing at a person directly.
normal.cn: 较早的义项是「按名字、指名地」，说明这个词最初是直接指向某个人的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker pausing, then putting a finger on the vague word and writing the real name under it.
abstract.cn: 想像说话人停顿一下，把手指按在笼统的词上，在它下面写出真正的名字。

abstract.en: A list after namely is not extra information; it is the unpacking of a single word that was too broad.
abstract.cn: namely 后面的清单不是补充信息，而是把一个过于宽泛的词拆开摆出来。

abstract.en: The word is exactness itself, which is why it sounds stiff in speech and natural in definitions and contracts.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是「精确」本身，所以它在口语里显得生硬，在定义和合同里却很自然。

examples.en: Only one person can sign the contract, namely the owner.
examples.cn: 合同只能由一个人签，也就是业主本人。

examples.en: Two countries signed the treaty, namely France and Spain.
examples.cn: 两个国家签署了这项条约，即法国和西班牙。

examples.en: He gave two reasons, namely cost and time.
examples.cn: 他给了两个理由，即成本和时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内姆里」——把话里那个笼统的说法点出名字来；记住 namely 是即、也就是。

root: 由 name（名字）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，-ly 源自古英语副词词尾 -lice，最初表示「按名字、指名地」，后收窄为「也就是说」。

sensesIntro.en: There are two uses rather than many senses: one points at a single exact term, the other unpacks a group into its named parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词只有两种用法而不是许多义项：一种指出单个确切词语，另一种把整体拆成一个个点名的部分。

definition_en: in a firm and even way, or in a way that continues without stopping
core_image: 匀速行走的秒针
scene: 雨稳稳地下了一整夜。 The rain fell steadily all night.
sceneCN: 这里 steadily 是「稳定地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雨稳稳地下了一整夜。

senses.title: In a firm way
senses.definition: in a firm, even, and controlled way
senses.definitionCN: 以稳固、均匀而有控制的方式
senses.example: The rain fell steadily all night.
senses.exampleCN: 雨稳稳地下了一整夜。
senses.why: The basic sense is firmness without shaking.
senses.whyCN: 基本义是稳固而不摇晃。

senses.title: Without stopping
senses.definition: in a way that continues over time without stopping
senses.definitionCN: 随时间不停继续的方式
senses.example: Prices have risen steadily for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 物价持续上涨了一年。
senses.why: Something firm can also keep going.
senses.whyCN: 稳固的东西，也能一直持续下去。

senses.title: Step by step
senses.definition: in a gradual and sure way
senses.definitionCN: 以渐进且有把握的方式
senses.example: She is steadily improving her English.
senses.exampleCN: 她的英语在稳步提高。
senses.why: Steady movement is movement that does not slip back.
senses.whyCN: 稳步前进，就是不倒退的前进。

items.cn: steady 意为稳固而均匀。

items.en: It described continued, gradual change.

note.en: Steadily is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of steady movement.

definition_en: to move continuously around a closed system, to pass from person to person, or to send something to many people
core_image: 红色的血在管道里一圈圈地流动
scene: 屋里暖气开得足，空气闷得发沉。 Open the window so the air can circulate.
sceneCN: 这里 circulate 指「循环」（第 1 个义项：流体沿闭合系统不断流动）；句意是打开窗户，让空气流通。

senses.title: To move in a loop
senses.definition: to move continuously around a closed system
senses.definitionCN: 沿闭合系统不断流动
senses.example: Blood circulates through the body.
senses.exampleCN: 血液在全身循环。
senses.why: Latin circulare meant to make a ring, and the ring became a path of flow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circulare 意为使成环，圆环随后成了流动的路径。

senses.title: To pass from person to person
senses.definition: to pass from one person or place to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一人或一处传到另一人另一处
senses.example: The rumour circulated quickly through the office.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言很快在办公室里传开。
senses.why: Goods and news move in a loop through many hands, like liquid in a pipe.
senses.whyCN: 货物与消息像管中液体一样，经许多手绕行流动。

senses.title: To send round to readers
senses.definition: to send something to a number of people in turn
senses.definitionCN: 把某物依次发给若干人
senses.example: The department circulated the draft to all staff.
senses.exampleCN: 部门把草稿传阅给全体员工。
senses.why: Sending a paper round repeats the same circular motion in paper form.
senses.whyCN: 把文件绕着发送，正是以纸张形式重复同一种环形运动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with goods changing hands at a port, then move to the wider world of business.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从港口上货物易手开始，再走到更广阔的商界。

normal.en: The Latin merx means goods, so commerce is goods moving together.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merx 意为货物，所以 commerce 就是货物一起流动。

normal.en: Commerce is uncountable: you never say a commerce.
normal.cn: commerce 不可数：不能说「一个商业」。

normal.en: A chamber of commerce is a group of traders, not a room of goods.
normal.cn: 商会是商人组成的团体，并不是堆货的房间。

normal.en: Electronic commerce moved the market onto screens.
normal.cn: 电子商务把市场搬到了屏幕上。

normal.en: Commerce and commercial share the same stem, one noun and one adjective.
normal.cn: commerce 与 commercial 同干，一个是名词，一个是形容词。

abstract.en: Picture crates swinging from a crane onto a dock.
abstract.cn: 想象货箱被吊车吊上码头。

abstract.en: Picture two merchants shaking hands over a price.
abstract.cn: 想象两个商人就价格握手成交。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour lit all night by lanterns and trade.
abstract.cn: 想象一座整夜被灯火与买卖照亮的港口。

examples.en: Trade and commerce built this harbour town.
examples.cn: 贸易与商业造就了这座港口小城。

examples.en: Electronic commerce has changed how people shop.
examples.cn: 电子商务改变了人们购物的方式。

examples.en: The two countries signed a treaty on commerce.
examples.cn: 两国签署了一项商业条约。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 commerce 记成 com（一起）加 merce（货物）：货物一起来回流动，就是商业。

root: 源自拉丁语 commercium（互相交易），词根 merx 意为货物，本义是货物的交换，后泛指商业与商务。

sensesIntro.en: From goods changing hands on a large scale, to the whole world of business.
sensesIntro.cn: 从大规模地货物易手，到整个商业世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a busy harbour where crates, ships and merchants keep moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：港口上货船靠岸、买家与卖家讨价还价的喧闹。

branches.en: The trade sense is the oldest and still the core.
branches.cn: 贸易义最古老，至今仍是核心。

branches.en: The activity widened into a whole social world.
branches.cn: 这种活动扩展成了一个完整的社会领域。

branches.en: Every trade deal is also a small act of business life.
branches.cn: 每一笔交易同时也是商务生活中的一个小动作。

branches.en: Ports and offices are two scenes of the same word.
branches.cn: 港口与写字楼是同一个词的两个场景。

branches.en: Commerce today includes clicks as well as crates.
branches.cn: 今天的商业既有鼠标点击，也有货箱。

intro.en: Commerce is a free base whose family grows with -ial, -ialize and -ially.
intro.cn: commerce 是自由词基，家族靠 -ial、-ialize 与 -ially 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root merc- for goods also appears in merchant and market.
latinIntro.cn: 表示货物的拉丁词根 merc- 也出现在 merchant 与 market 之中。

items.example: The area is a commercial centre.
The channel runs too many commercials.
items.exampleCN: 这个频道播的广告太多了。
他们把这个古老节日商业化了。

items.example: The beach has become fully commercialized.
items.exampleCN: 这片海滩已经完全商业化。

items.example: The film was not commercially successful.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片在商业上并不成功。

items.example: Critics blame commercialism for the change.
items.exampleCN: 批评者把这一变化归咎于商业主义。

items.structure: related noun from the same root
items.meaning: a person who trades in goods
items.example: A merchant sold silk at the port.
items.exampleCN: 一位商人在港口卖丝绸。
去年电子商务增长很快。

definition_zh: 乐意地；自愿地；心甘情愿地
definition_en: in a way that shows you are ready and glad to do something, without being forced
core_image: 有人还没说完请求，听的人已经把袖子卷起来，笑着往前走了一步
scene: 搬家那天，她一喊，几个邻居没等把话讲完就卷起袖子下楼帮忙。 They willingly carried the heavy boxes up four floors without a word of complaint.
sceneCN: 这里 willingly 是「乐意地」（第 1 个义项：自愿且痛快地做某事）；句意为他们心甘情愿地把沉重的箱子搬上四层楼，一句怨言也没有。卷起袖子笑着往前那一步，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: With a glad heart
senses.definition: in a ready and cheerful way, with no sign of being pushed into it
senses.definitionCN: 带着愿意且愉快的心情，没有一点被逼迫的样子
senses.example: They willingly carried the heavy boxes up four floors without a word of complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他们心甘情愿地把沉重的箱子搬上四层楼，一句怨言也没有。
senses.why: The adverb simply turns the inner readiness of will into the way an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是把内心那份愿意，变成做事的姿态。

senses.title: Of one's own free choice
senses.definition: by personal choice rather than because a rule or a person demands it
senses.definitionCN: 出于个人选择，而不是因为规定或他人要求
senses.example: She willingly gave up her seat to the old man on the crowded bus.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的公交车上，她自愿把座位让给了那位老人。
senses.why: Readiness can also mean that nobody asked at all, so the word covers free giving.
senses.whyCN: 愿意有时也意味着根本没人开口，于是这个词也涵盖主动给予。

senses.title: Without payment or pressure
senses.definition: in a way that serves others without expecting money or reward, as in the usual phrase
senses.definitionCN: 在为他人做事而不图钱或回报时使用，常用于固定说法
senses.example: Many retired teachers willingly spend their mornings helping children read.
senses.exampleCN: 许多退休教师心甘情愿地花上午的时间教孩子读书。
senses.why: When readiness costs nothing to the giver, it lines up with the unpaid service of volunteers.
senses.whyCN: 当这份愿意对付出者毫无价钱时，它就与志愿者的无偿服务重合了。

intro.en: Willingly is the adverb built on willing, which comes from the noun will, the faculty of choosing; the root is Old English willan, to wish.
intro.cn: willingly 是由 willing 构成的副词，willing 出自名词 will（选择的能力），词根是古英语 willan（希望、愿意）。

items.en: willan meant to wish or to desire, and willa was the mind that wishes.
items.cn: willan 表示希望、渴望，willa 指那颗愿想的心。

items.en: The adjective willende described someone full of intention, close to today's willing.
items.cn: 形容词 willende 形容一个人满怀意愿，与今天的 willing 很接近。

items.en: The ending shifted to -ing and the word settled as willing, ready to do something.
items.cn: 词尾变成 -ing，这个词固定为 willing，意为愿意去做某事。

items.en: The adverb ending gave willingly, first with the sense of acting by choice.
items.cn: 加上副词词尾得到 willingly，最初表示出于选择而行动。

items.en: Today the word carries a warm tone, suggesting the person is glad rather than merely obedient.
items.cn: 今天这个词带有温和的色彩，暗示此人是高兴的，而不只是顺从。

note.en: The first group holds near twins formed from the same stem, the second holds other adverbs of cheerful consent.
note.cn: 第一组收同根而生、模样相近的词，第二组收其他表示欣然同意的副词。

entries.definition: Ready to do something when asked.
The state of being ready to help.
Doing something with clear reluctance.
Deliberately, often against what is right.
With pleasure, happily.
Willingly and without delay.
By free choice, with no one forcing you.

normalIntro.en: Willingly is will plus -ing plus -ly, so the spelling is only long because it shows the inner choice twice.
normalIntro.cn: willingly 是 will 加 -ing 再加 -ly，拼写之所以长，是因为它把内心那份选择说了两遍。

normal.en: Keep the double l from will, then add ing, then add ly.
normal.cn: 先保留 will 的两个 l，再加 ing，最后加 ly。

normal.en: Willing is the person who says yes with the whole face.
normal.cn: willing 就是整张脸都在说「好」的那个人。

normal.en: The tail -ly marks the manner: how the yes was given.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 标记方式：那个「好」是怎么说出口的。

normal.en: Unwillingly wears the negative hat un-, and drops it to become gladly willing.
normal.cn: unwillingly 戴着否定帽子 un-，摘掉它就变成欣然愿意。

normal.en: Link it to willpower: the same will that decides also drives the glad step.
normal.cn: 把它和意志力联系起来：做决定的那份意志，也推动了愉快的那一步。

abstract.en: A hand reaching for the box before the request is finished.
abstract.cn: 一句请求还没说完，一只手已经伸向那只箱子。

abstract.en: A face opening like a door, no shadow of being pushed.
abstract.cn: 一张像门一样打开的脸，没有半点被推着走的阴影。

abstract.en: Weight accepted as if it were light.
abstract.cn: 重量被接过来，轻得像不存在。

examples.en: He willingly took the night shift so his colleague could go home.
examples.cn: 他自愿接下夜班，好让同事能回家。

examples.en: The children willingly shared their toys with the new boy.
examples.cn: 孩子们乐意把玩具分享给新来的男孩。

examples.en: Nobody promised her money, yet she willingly came every weekend.
examples.cn: 没人许诺给她钱，她却每个周末都心甘情愿地来。

dict_mnemonic.text: will（意愿）+ ing + ly —— 带着意愿去做，就是「乐意地」。

root: 古英语 willan（希望、愿意）→ willa（心意）→ willing（愿意的）→ willingly；同族有 willingness、unwilling。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from a glad heart to a free choice, and finally to a service that asks for no money.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一颗乐意的心，走到自由的选择，最后走到不求报酬的服务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand already reaching out before the request ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：请求还没说完，手已经伸了出去。

branches.en: The glad branch: boxes carried up four floors with a smile.
branches.cn: 乐意分支：笑着把箱子搬上四层。

branches.en: The free branch: a seat given up on a crowded bus.
branches.cn: 自愿分支：在拥挤的车上让出座位。

branches.en: The unpaid branch: retired teachers offering their mornings.
branches.cn: 无偿分支：退休教师献出自己的上午。

branches.en: The manner branch: the adverb colours how the choice is carried out.
branches.cn: 方式分支：副词为选择如何落实涂上色彩。

branches.en: The character branch: a readiness that has become a habit.
branches.cn: 品性分支：愿意已经变成习惯。

intro.en: Willingly is a stack of native pieces: the stem will, the adjective ending -ing and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: willingly 由几个本土成分叠成：词干 will、形容词词尾 -ing 和副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The stem is native Germanic, so there is no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below are borrowed cousins only.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词只是借入的表亲。

items.meaning: the power to choose or wish
items.example: It is the plain core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词朴素的核心。
它由 will 构成 willing。
它由 willing 构成 willingly。

items.example: The noun keeps the warm tone.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留了温和的语气。

items.example: The same stem turns cold here.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词干在这里变得冰冷。

definition_zh: 删节；节略；缩短；剥夺（权利）
definition_en: to make a text, speech, or period shorter, or to cut down a right or freedom
core_image: 一把红笔在厚书上划掉整段，书页变薄
scene: 出版社的编辑桌上堆着一部厚厚的长篇小说，红笔已经划掉了几十页。 The publisher abridged the long novel for young readers.
sceneCN: 这里 abridge 是「删节文字作品」（第 1 个义项：删去部分内容使篇幅变短）；句意为出版社为年轻读者删节了这部长篇小说。

pos.zh: 及物动词：删节；节略；缩短；剥夺；限制

derivatives.zh: 由 abridge 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「删节；节略本」
由 abridge 加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「删节过的、简略的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 abridged 构成，义为「未删节的、完整的」
由 abridge 加施动后缀 -er 构成，义为「删节者」

senses.title: To shorten a text by cutting parts
senses.definition: to shorten a book, article, or other text by removing parts of it
senses.definitionCN: 删去书、文章或其他文本的部分内容，使其变短
senses.example: The publisher abridged the long novel for young readers.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社为年轻读者删节了这部长篇小说。
senses.why: breviare, from brevis 'short', is the root; cutting a text is the plainest way to make it short.
senses.whyCN: 词根 breviare 出自 brevis「短」；把文本删掉一部分，正是让它变短最直白的方式。

senses.title: To produce a shortened edition
senses.definition: to prepare a shorter version of a work for publication or performance
senses.definitionCN: 为出版或演出准备一个篇幅更短的版本
senses.example: The play was abridged for a single evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这个剧本被压缩成一场晚会能演完的版本。
senses.why: Here the cutting serves a fixed frame: the edition must fit a page count or a stage time.
senses.whyCN: 这里的删减服务于一个固定框架：版本必须装进规定的页数或演出时长。

senses.title: To shorten a speech or statement
senses.definition: to make a speech, report, or statement shorter
senses.definitionCN: 使讲话、报告或陈述变得更短
senses.example: She abridged her remarks to ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她把发言压缩到十分钟。
senses.why: Spoken words are cut the same way written ones are: the material is shortened before delivery.
senses.whyCN: 口头的话语与书面文字一样被剪短：材料在说出之前就被压缩。

senses.title: To shorten a period of time
senses.definition: to make a period or process shorter in duration
senses.definitionCN: 使一段时间或过程持续得更短
senses.example: The new route abridges the journey by an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 新路线把行程缩短了一个小时。
senses.why: If a stretch of time is a length, it can be cut like a page; the metaphor is one of measured extent.
senses.whyCN: 如果把一段时间看作一段长度，它就能像书页一样被剪短；这个比喻建立在「可量的长度」上。

senses.title: To shorten a distance or way
senses.definition: to make a distance or route shorter, an older sense still found in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 使距离或路线变短，这一较旧的义项仍见于正式书面语
senses.example: A tunnel would abridge the road between the two towns.
senses.exampleCN: 一条隧道会缩短两镇之间的路程。
senses.why: A road is a line on the ground; cutting it short is the spatial version of the same shortening.
senses.whyCN: 道路是地面上的一条线；把它截短，是同一个「缩短」在空间上的版本。

senses.title: To condense to the essential points
senses.definition: to reduce material to its essential points without losing the main sense
senses.definitionCN: 把材料压缩到要点，同时不丢失主要意思
senses.example: The summary abridges three chapters into one page.
senses.exampleCN: 这份摘要把三章内容压缩成一页。
senses.why: Shortening well is not random deletion: what remains must still carry the whole, so the cut is a condensation.
senses.whyCN: 好的删节不是随意删除：留下来的部分仍要承载整体，所以这种剪切是一种浓缩。

senses.title: To deprive someone of a right
senses.definition: in law, to deprive a person of a right, privilege, or benefit
senses.definitionCN: 法律用语，指剥夺某人的权利、特权或利益
senses.example: The old statute abridged the rights of tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧法令剥夺了租户的权利。
senses.why: A right is treated as something a person holds; cutting it off leaves the holder with less than before.
senses.whyCN: 权利被当作人手里握有的东西；把它切掉，持有人就比原来少了。

senses.title: To limit freedom or power
senses.definition: to restrict or cut down a freedom, power, or authority
senses.definitionCN: 限制或削减自由、权力或权威
senses.example: No law may abridge freedom of speech.
senses.exampleCN: 任何法律都不得限制言论自由。
senses.why: The legal sense widens from a single right to any freedom: whatever is cut down is abridged.
senses.whyCN: 法律义从单项权利扩展到任何自由：凡是被削减的，就是被 abridge。

intro.en: Abridge came through Old French from a Late Latin verb built on the adjective brevis, 'short'.
intro.cn: abridge 经古法语来自一个晚期拉丁动词，其词根是形容词 brevis「短的」。

items.en: brevis meant short or brief, and it is the source of English brief and brevity.
items.cn: brevis 意为「短的、简短的」，是英语 brief 与 brevity 的来源。

items.en: breviare, 'to shorten', was formed from brevis; with ad- it became abbreviare.
items.cn: breviare「缩短」由 brevis 构成；加上 ad- 后成为 abbreviare。

items.en: Late Latin abbreviare, 'to shorten', passed into Old French as abregier.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 abbreviare「缩短」传入古法语，成为 abregier。

items.en: Old French abregier carried the word into Middle English as abreggen.
items.cn: 古法语 abregier 把这个词带入中古英语，作 abreggen。

items.en: English abridge is recorded from the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 abridge 自十四世纪起有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the brevity family and the longer Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of cutting and condensing.
note.cn: 形近组收 brevity 词族与较长的拉丁词干；近义组收表示剪切与压缩的动词。

entries.definition: The act of shortening a text, or the shortened text itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「删节；节略本」，由 abridge 加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: Shortened by having parts removed, of a text or edition.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「删节过的」，由 abridge 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Complete, with nothing removed; the opposite of abridged.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未删节的、完整的」，由 un- 加 abridged 构成。

entries.definition: To shorten a word, phrase, or text, from the same Latin brevis.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩写、缩短」，与 abridge 同出拉丁语 brevis「短」。

entries.definition: Shortness of speech or writing, from Latin brevitas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「简短、简洁」，同样出自 brevis，但只指风格上的短。

entries.definition: To make something shorter in length, time, or duration; the most general word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使变短」，用于长度、时间或篇幅，是最一般的说法。

entries.definition: To make a text or substance denser by reducing what is in it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「压缩、浓缩」，强调减少内容或体积后更紧凑。

entries.definition: To cut off the end of something, especially in computing or geometry.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「截断、截短」，多用于计算机或几何，强调去掉末端。

entries.definition: To reduce or cut short a right, spending, or an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「削减、缩短」，多用于权利、开支或活动，语气正式。

entries.definition: To remove part of a text, film, or budget; the everyday verb behind abridge.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「删剪、削减」，是 abridge 背后最日常的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root brevis and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 brevis，以及这个词出现的搭配。

normal.en: brevis is Latin for short: abridge is to make short.
normal.cn: brevis 是拉丁语的「短」：abridge 就是使变短。

normal.en: abbreviate and brevity come from the same brevis, so the family shares one idea.
normal.cn: abbreviate 与 brevity 同出 brevis，整个词族共享一个「短」的念头。

normal.en: An abridged edition cuts a text; an unabridged one keeps every word.
normal.cn: abridged edition 删节文本；unabridged 版本则一字不减。

normal.en: abridgement is the noun for both the act and the shortened version.
normal.cn: abridgement 既是「删节」这个动作，也指删节后的版本。

normal.en: In law, to abridge a right is to cut it short.
normal.cn: 在法律里，abridge a right 就是把一项权利切短。

abstract.en: Picture a thick book with a pair of scissors laid beside it: the cut pages are what disappear.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书旁边放着一把剪刀：消失的正是被剪下的书页。

abstract.en: The same scissors can cut a speech, a journey, a timetable or a legal right.
abstract.cn: 同一把剪刀可以剪短讲话、旅程、时间表，也可以剪掉一项法律权利。

abstract.en: Good abridging keeps the shape of the whole while removing what can be spared.
abstract.cn: 好的删节保留整体的形状，只去掉可以省去的部分。

examples.en: The editors abridged the report to four pages.
examples.cn: 编辑把报告删节到四页。

examples.en: This is the abridged edition, not the full text.
examples.cn: 这是节略本，不是全文。

examples.en: The court ruled that the new rule abridged free speech.

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all shorten something: a text, an edition, a speech, a period, a route, a summary, a right, or a freedom.

branches.en: THE EDITION: a shorter version is made for a fixed frame, keeping the essential points.

branches.en: THE SPEECH: spoken words are cut short before they are delivered.

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a period of time or a route is shortened as if it were a length.
branches.cn: 度量线：一段时间或一条路线像长度一样被截短。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: law cuts down a right, a freedom, or a power.

definition_zh: 分配；指派；确定（时间、地点）
definition_en: to give a task or share to someone, or to fix a time, place or right
core_image: 名册上每个名字旁边写着分到的那一份
scene: 编辑部的白板上写着各人负责的栏目。 She was assigned to the travel desk.
sceneCN: 这里 assign 是「指派」（第 1 个义项：把任务分给某人）；句意是她被派去负责旅游版。

senses.title: Give a task or share
senses.definition: to give someone a particular job or a share of something
senses.definitionCN: 把某项工作或某一份东西交给某人
senses.example: She was assigned to the travel desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她被派去负责旅游版。
senses.why: Assign comes from Latin assignare 'to mark out', the act of noting on a list that a thing belongs to a certain person, so the sense is a marked allotment.
senses.whyCN: assign 源自拉丁语 assignare「作标记」，原指在名册上标明某物归谁，因此核心是「标好归属的分派」。

senses.title: Fix a time or place
senses.definition: to decide and state a time, place or value
senses.definitionCN: 确定并说明时间、地点或数值
senses.example: The judge assigned a date for the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 法官确定了听证日期。
senses.why: Marking on a list also served to pin down when and where something happens, so 'allot' extended to fixing a date or place.
senses.whyCN: 在名册上作标记同样用于给日子和地点定位，于是「分派」自然引申为把时间、地点确定下来。

senses.title: Transfer by law
senses.definition: to transfer property or a right to another person in law
senses.definitionCN: 依法把财产或权利转到他人名下
senses.example: He assigned the copyright to the publisher.
senses.exampleCN: 他把版权转让给了出版社。
senses.why: Writing a right under another person's name is the most literal form of the marking act, and law kept that concrete sense as 'transfer'.
senses.whyCN: 把一项权利登记到别人名下，是「作标记」最字面的一种做法，法律保留了这个具体含义，用作「转让」。

senses.why: A thing your hand can hold cannot be argued away by words.

senses.why: Soft wet stone sets into one body, and that body carries weight.

definition_en: a field or area of activity, knowledge or interest; a kingdom or country ruled by a monarch; a major division of the natural world

scene: 地图摊在桌上，边界线把一片土地清清楚楚地围起来。 The realm of insects is far larger than most people imagine.
sceneCN: 这里 realm 是「领域」（第 1 个义项：某一活动或知识的范围）；句意为昆虫的领域远比多数人想象的大。画面里可留意：摊开的地图、清楚的边界线、围起的土地。

senses.title: A field or area
senses.definition: a field or area of activity, knowledge or interest
senses.definitionCN: 活动、知识或兴趣的一个范围
senses.example: The realm of insects is far larger than most people imagine.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫的领域远比多数人想象的大。
senses.why: A realm was first a territory with borders, and a field of study is also a territory with borders, so the word extended to knowledge.
senses.whyCN: realm 最初指有边界的领土，而一个研究领域也是有边界的领土，于是这个词扩展到知识。

senses.title: A kingdom
senses.definition: a country or kingdom ruled by a monarch
senses.definitionCN: 由君主统治的国家或王国
senses.example: The old realm was divided among three kings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老的王国被三位国王瓜分。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a land under a ruler, the territory that a king actually governs.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「君主统治下的土地」，即国王实际治理的疆域。

senses.title: A division of nature
senses.definition: one of the great divisions of the natural world, such as animals, plants or fungi
senses.definitionCN: 自然世界的主要划分之一，如动物界、植物界或真菌界
senses.example: Fungi form a realm of their own, neither plant nor animal.
senses.exampleCN: 真菌自成—界，既非植物也非动物。
senses.why: Science borrowed the word for the largest divisions of living things, because each is a territory with its own borders.
senses.whyCN: 科学借这个词指生物最大的几大划分，因为每一界都是有自身边界的领土。

intro.en: Realm comes from Old French reaume, a kingdom, from Latin regimen, rule, and regere, to rule; English narrowed the spelling but kept the territory.
intro.cn: realm 来自古法语 reaume（王国），源于拉丁语 regimen（统治）与 regere（统治）；英语改变了拼写，却保留了「领土」之意。

items.en: Regere meant to rule or guide straight, and it is the source of regal, regime and region as well.
items.cn: regere 意为统治或引直，也是 regal、regime、region 的来源。

items.en: Regimen meant rule or government, the act by which a territory is held.
items.cn: regimen 意为统治或治理，是维系一片领土的行为。

items.en: Old French reaume named the kingdom itself, the land that a ruler governs.
items.cn: 古法语 reaume 命名王国本身，即统治者所治理的土地。

items.en: Middle English shortened the spelling toward realm but kept the sense of a ruled territory.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写缩短为 realm，但保留「被统治的领土」之意。

items.en: Modern English uses realm for a kingdom, for any bounded field of activity, and for a division of nature.
items.cn: 现代英语用 realm 指王国、任何有边界的活动领域，以及自然界的一大划分。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same ruling root; the near-meaning group gathers words for territory and field.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「统治」词根的词；近义组收表示领土与范围的词。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a ruled territory, then becomes any bounded field, and finally a great division of nature.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「被统治的领土」开始，随后成为任何有边界的领域，最后成为自然界的一大划分。

normal.en: Realm, regal, regime and region all come from the Latin word for rule.
normal.cn: realm、regal、regime、region 都来自拉丁语中表示「统治」的词。

normal.en: A realm is a territory with borders, whether a kingdom or a field of study.
normal.cn: realm 是有边界的领土，可以是王国，也可以是研究领域。

normal.en: The realm of nature is a phrase for the whole living world.
normal.cn: the realm of nature 指整个生命世界的说法。

normal.en: Within the realm of is the phrase for saying what an idea belongs to.
normal.cn: within the realm of 是用来说明某观念属于哪个范围的短语。

normal.en: A realm can be expanded, as a kingdom adds land or a science adds subjects.
normal.cn: realm 可以扩展，正如王国增添土地、科学增添科目。

abstract.en: Every realm is made by the border drawn around it.
abstract.cn: 每一个 realm 都由围在它周围的边界造成。

abstract.en: To enter a new realm is to accept its rules.
abstract.cn: 进入一个新的领域，就是接受它的规则。

abstract.en: The realm of the possible is wider than the realm of the permitted.
abstract.cn: 可能的领域比被允许的领域更宽。

examples.cn: 真菌自成一界，既非植物也非动物。

branches.cn: 与动植物分开的真菌

branches.cn: 研究领域与王国，都有边界

branches.cn: 土地的王國与生物的王國

latinIntro.en: Latin regere, to rule, and regimen, rule, are the recorded sources of the family.

definition_en: the amount of matter or people in a given space, or the strength of something mixed in liquid
core_image: 同样大的方格里，一边放了三颗豆，一边塞了三十颗
scene: 老师往两个同样大的盒子里装豆子，一个很快装满，另一个还空着大半。 The density of the city makes land very expensive.
sceneCN: 这里 density 指「密度」（第 1 个义项：单位空间里所含的量）；句意是这座城市的密度让土地变得非常昂贵。

senses.title: Mass in a given space
senses.definition: the amount of matter in a given space
senses.definitionCN: 一定空间内所含物质的量
senses.example: Lead has a much higher density than wood.
senses.exampleCN: 铅的密度比木头高得多。
senses.why: Density answers one question: how much in how little room.
senses.whyCN: 密度只回答一个问题：多小的空间里装了多少。

senses.title: Crowding of people or traffic
senses.definition: the state of people or vehicles being crowded together
senses.definitionCN: 人或车辆拥挤在一起的状态
senses.example: The density of traffic slows every bus.
senses.exampleCN: 交通的密度让每辆公交都变慢。
senses.why: A street can be measured the way a block of metal is measured.
senses.whyCN: 街道也能像一块金属那样被量出疏密。

senses.title: Strength of a mixture
senses.definition: the strength of a substance mixed into a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 某物质在液体中的浓度
senses.example: They measured the density of salt in the water.
senses.exampleCN: 他们测量了水中盐的浓度。
senses.why: Salt leaves no shape, so only its density can be counted.
senses.whyCN: 盐没有形状，只能靠浓度来计数。

intro.en: Density is Latin densitas, the quality of being densus, thick or crowded, plus the noun ending -ity.
intro.cn: density 是拉丁语 densitas，表示 densus（浓密、拥挤）这种性质，后面带上名词词尾 -ity。

items.en: Densus described thick woods, heavy fog and packed ranks.
items.cn: densus 形容茂密的树林、浓重的雾与挤紧的队列。

items.en: Densitas named the quality itself rather than the thing.
items.cn: densitas 指这种性质本身，而不是那样东西。

items.en: Science gave density a number: mass divided by volume.
items.cn: 科学给了密度一个数字：质量除以体积。

items.en: Cities and crowds began to be described by density too.
items.cn: 城市与人群也开始用密度来描述。

items.en: It now measures matter, people and even traffic.
items.cn: 如今它既量物质，也量人，甚至量交通。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dens- stem, and the meaning group gives three measures of how much is packed in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dens- 词干，近义组则给出三种衡量「装了多少」的说法。

entries.definition: packed closely together
in a closely packed way
to make something smaller or thicker
the amount of a substance in a mixture
entries.definitionCN: 混合物中某物质的含量

entries.definition: the distance between two sides
the state of too many things in one place
entries.definitionCN: 太多东西挤在一处的状态

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two boxes of beans and end with salt that disappears into water.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两盒豆子开始，落到盐溶进水里看不见。

normal.en: Same box, more beans: that is density in one picture.
normal.cn: 一样的盒子，装进更多豆子，这就是密度。

normal.en: Density is a fraction: what you have over the room it takes.
normal.cn: 密度是一个分数：有多少东西，除以它占的空间。

normal.en: A crowded train and a heavy metal share the same word.
normal.cn: 拥挤的列车与沉重的金属共用一个词。

normal.en: Salt in water keeps its density but loses its shape.
normal.cn: 盐在水里保住了浓度，却丢了形状。

normal.en: Add -ity to dense and the quality becomes countable.
normal.cn: dense 后面加 -ity，性质就变得可以计数。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon that stands upright in thick honey.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子直立在浓稠的蜂蜜里。

abstract.en: Picture a square metre of ground with thirty people on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一平方米的地上站了三十个人。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of water turning faintly salty.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水慢慢有了淡淡的咸味。

examples.en: Lead has a much higher density than wood.
examples.cn: 铅的密度比木头高得多。

examples.en: They measured the density of salt in the water.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 density 记成「凳子 city」：一座城里凳子的数量除以城的面积，就是密度。

root: 来自拉丁语 densitas，由 densus（浓密、拥挤）加名词词尾 -ity 构成。它先把「稠密」当成一种性质，十七世纪科学又把它变成可计算的量：质量除以体积；后来城市、人群与交通也用它来衡量。

sensesIntro.en: From beans in a box, to matter on a scale, to people in a street, to salt in water.
sensesIntro.cn: 从盒里的豆子，到秤上的物质，到街上的人，再到水里的盐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same box holds far more beans when they are packed tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个盒子，豆子挤紧后能装下多得多。

branches.en: The first sense is a number for matter in a space.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是空间里物质含量的数字。

branches.en: The second sense applies the same number to people and vehicles.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把同一个数字用在人与车辆上。

branches.en: The third sense measures what has dissolved out of sight.
branches.cn: 第三个义项衡量溶进水里、看不见的东西。

branches.en: Metal and traffic are both judged by how much fits in one place.
branches.cn: 金属与交通，都按一处能装多少来评判。

branches.en: A crowded street and a strong solution are both thick with something.
branches.cn: 拥挤的街道与浓溶液，都因为某样东西太多而变稠。

intro.en: Density sits at the centre of a family that runs from the adjective dense to verbs of pressing and measuring.
intro.cn: density 位于一个家族的中心，从形容词 dense 一直连到表示压紧与测量的动词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin densus, thick or crowded, with -ity naming the quality.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 densus（浓密、拥挤），-ity 把这种性质变成名词。

items.example: They densified the soil before building.
items.exampleCN: 他们建房前把土压得更实。

definition_zh: 匿名的；无名的；毫无特色的
definition_en: having no name given or known, or lacking any distinctive character
core_image: 信末空着的签名处
scene: 信封里没有落款，只有一张打印的纸。 The donation came from an anonymous reader.
sceneCN: 这里 anonymous 是「匿名的」（第 1 个义项：不署名的）；句意是这笔捐款来自一位匿名读者。

pos.zh: 形容词：匿名的；无名的；无特色的

senses.title: With no name given
senses.definition: written, given, or done by someone who does not reveal their name
senses.definitionCN: 由不透露姓名的人所写、所给或所做的
senses.example: The donation came from an anonymous reader.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔捐款来自一位匿名读者。
senses.why: Greek an- means 'without' and onoma means 'name', so anonymous literally describes something that arrives without a name attached.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 an- 意为「无」，onoma 意为「名字」，所以 anonymous 字面就是指送来时没有附上名字的东西。

senses.title: With no known author
senses.definition: used of a work or person whose name is unknown rather than deliberately withheld
senses.definitionCN: 用于作品或人，其名字是不为人知，而非有意隐去
senses.example: The painting was long thought to be by an anonymous artist.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画长期被认为出自一位无名画家之手。
senses.why: The same word covers both hiding a name and simply not knowing it, because in either case no name is available.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指隐去名字，也指根本不知道名字，因为两种情况下都拿不到名字。

senses.title: Without distinctive character
senses.definition: lacking any feature that would make a place, object, or experience memorable
senses.definitionCN: 缺少任何能让地方、物件或经历留下印象的特点
senses.example: They spent the night in an anonymous hotel near the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在机场附近一家毫无特色的旅馆过了一夜。
senses.why: If a thing has no name you can recall, it feels interchangeable, and that feeling of facelessness is the extended sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西没有你能记住的名字，它就显得可以随便替换，这种面目模糊的感觉就是延伸义。

intro.en: Anonymous is Greek for 'nameless', rebuilt in English from Latin.
intro.cn: anonymous 在希腊语中意为「无名的」，英语中是经由拉丁语重新拼成的。

items.en: onoma meant 'name', the root of many English name-words.
items.cn: onoma 意为「名字」，是许多英语名字类词的词根。

items.en: anonymos meant 'without a name', built with the prefix an-.
items.cn: anonymos 意为「没有名字的」，由前缀 an- 构成。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective almost unchanged.
items.cn: 拉丁语几乎原样接收了这个希腊形容词。

items.en: English anonymous first described books with no author named.
items.cn: 英语 anonymous 最初形容未署作者名的书。

items.en: The sense of 'faceless, without character' developed in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 「面目模糊、毫无特色」的义项在二十世纪发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group plays on the name-root; the near-meaning group covers ways of not being identified.
note.cn: 形近组围绕「名字」词根做文章；近义组是各种不被识别的说法。

definition_en: an open space surrounded by the walls of a building or buildings
core_image: 四面房子围出一块方地，中间种着一棵小树
scene: 推开木门，四面都是房，中间那块空地种着一棵小树。 Children ran around the courtyard after dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 courtyard 指「庭院」（第 1 个义项：被房屋四面围住的空地）；句意是晚饭后孩子们在庭院里跑来跑去。

senses.title: A yard inside the walls
senses.definition: an open area surrounded by the walls of a building
senses.definitionCN: 被建筑物墙体围住的空地
senses.example: The old house has a stone courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老房子有一个石头庭院。
senses.why: Four walls turn a piece of sky into a private room.
senses.whyCN: 四面墙把一块天空围成一间私人的屋子。

senses.title: The air well of a big building
senses.definition: a narrow open space inside a large building that lets in light and air

intro.en: Courtyard joins court, from Latin cohors, an enclosed yard, with yard, from Old English geard, a fenced ground.
intro.cn: courtyard 由 court（源自拉丁语 cohors，围起的院子）与 yard（源自古英语 geard，围起的地）合成。

items.en: Cohors meant an enclosed yard or a guard.
items.cn: cohors 意为围起的院子或卫队。

items.en: Geard meant a fenced piece of ground.
items.cn: geard 意为用篱笆围起的一块地。

items.en: Court named the yard of a castle.
items.cn: court 指城堡里的院子。

items.en: Courtyard joined court and yard into one word.
items.cn: courtyard 把 court 与 yard 合成一个词。

items.en: It now names any open space closed in by walls.

definition_en: having a good effect on someone or something
core_image: 阳光落在刚发芽的幼苗上
scene: 晨光落在幼苗上，叶子慢慢舒展开。 Fresh air is beneficial to health.

senses.title: Good for health or growth
senses.definition: having a good effect on health or growth

senses.why: The core sense points to a good result for a living thing.

senses.title: Helpful to both sides

senses.exampleCN: 两家公司达成了互利的协议。

intro.cn: beneficial 来自拉丁语 bene facere，意为「做好事」。

items.cn: 法律用它指权利的享有者。

items.en: beneficial often pairs with to.
items.cn: 如今 beneficial 常与 to 搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -icial ending; the near-meaning group gives helpful words.

definition_zh: 砰地关上；猛烈抨击；砰的一声
definition_en: to shut something with great force or noise, or to criticize strongly
core_image: 门被用力关上，发出砰的一声
scene: 他气得砰地关上了门。 He slammed the door in anger.
sceneCN: 这里 slam 是「砰地关上」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他气得砰地关上了门。

derivatives.zh: 猛力关门的人；监狱（俚语）

senses.title: Shut with force
senses.definition: to shut a door or window with great force and noise
senses.definitionCN: 用力并带着响声关上门或窗
senses.example: He slammed the door in anger.
senses.exampleCN: 他气得砰地关上了门。
senses.why: This is the loud physical action.
senses.whyCN: 这是带响亮的实际动作。

senses.title: Criticize strongly
senses.definition: to criticize someone or something very strongly
senses.definitionCN: 非常严厉地批评某人或某事
senses.example: The report slammed the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告猛烈抨击了新政策。
senses.why: The force of a slam became verbal force.
senses.whyCN: 关门的猛劲变成了言语的猛烈。

senses.title: The loud impact
senses.definition: a loud noise made by something hitting or shutting hard
senses.definitionCN: 某物猛撞或猛关时发出的巨响
senses.example: We heard a loud slam from upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听到楼上传来砰的一声。
senses.why: The sound itself is named by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 声音本身也用同一个词来称呼。

intro.en: Slam probably came from a Scandinavian source.
intro.cn: slam 可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语。

items.en: A word for a heavy blow may be the source.
items.cn: 表示重击的词可能是其来源。

items.en: Slam appeared as a verb for noisy shutting.

items.en: It also meant to strike hard.

items.en: It widened to strong criticism.
items.cn: 词义扩展到严厉批评。

items.en: Sports gave it phrases like grand slam.

note.en: Slam is compared with look-alike words and words for impact.

sensesIntro.cn: slam 意为猛力关上、用言语猛烈抨击，或撞击的响声。

definition_en: as a result, or in a way that matches the situation
core_image: 暴雨预警亮起，运动会的日期在公告栏上被划掉改写
scene: 暴雨预警发布后，学校把原定的运动会改到下周。 The schedule was changed accordingly.
sceneCN: 这里的 accordingly 指「相应地」（第 2 个义项：按照新的情况作出对应调整）；句意是日程也相应改了。

senses.title: As a consequence
senses.definition: introduces a result that follows from what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 引出由前文所述自然产生的结果
senses.example: The road was flooded, and accordingly the match was called off.
senses.exampleCN: 道路被淹，比赛因此取消。
senses.why: The word grew out of according, meaning matching; a result that matches its cause follows from it, and that following is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由意为「相合」的 according 长出，与原因相合的结果自然随之而来，这层「随之」就是此义项。

senses.title: In a matching way
senses.definition: in the way that the new situation requires
senses.definitionCN: 按照变化后的情况作出对应的调整
senses.example: The schedule was changed accordingly.
senses.exampleCN: 日程也相应改了。
senses.why: When the action must fit the circumstance rather than follow from it, the same adverb means doing things to match.
senses.whyCN: 当动作是要去迎合情况、而不是由情况推出时，同一个副词就表示「照着调整」。

intro.en: The adverb is according with an ending that turns it into a word about manner.
intro.cn: 这个副词是 according 加上表示方式的词尾。

definition_en: wood prepared for building or carpentry, standing trees grown for that use, or a large beam in a structure

pos.zh: 名词：木材、木料；树木；横梁；人的素质

derivatives.zh: 加过去分词结尾，义为「木造的；有木材的」
加 -ing 名词化，义为「木支架；木材结构」

senses.title: Wood cut for building
senses.definition: wood that has been cut and prepared for use in building or carpentry
senses.definitionCN: 已锯好备用的建筑或木工用木材
senses.example: The barn was built from local timber.
senses.exampleCN: 这间谷仓是用本地的木材盖的。
senses.why: The Old English word first named a building or a structure, then the material that such structures were made from.
senses.whyCN: 古英语最初指建筑物、构造物，随后指建造这类构造所用的材料。

senses.title: Standing trees as a crop
senses.definition: forest trees considered as a resource to be harvested
senses.definitionCN: 被视为可采伐资源的森林树木
senses.example: The hillside timber was felled over one winter.
senses.exampleCN: 山坡上的林木在一个冬天里被砍伐。
senses.why: If cut wood is timber, then the trees waiting to be cut are timber too.
senses.whyCN: 如果锯下的木头是木材，那么等待被锯的树也算木材。

senses.title: A heavy beam
senses.definition: a large piece of shaped wood used as a beam in a structure
senses.definitionCN: 结构中用作梁的巨大木料
senses.example: One timber in the roof had rotted through.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶上有一根横梁已经烂穿。
senses.why: A beam is the cut wood at its most structural, carrying the weight of the building.
senses.whyCN: 横梁是木料最具结构性的形态，承担着建筑的重量。

senses.title: Wooden supports for a mine
senses.definition: the wooden props used to support tunnels in a mine
senses.definitionCN: 矿井中支撑巷道的木质支柱
senses.example: They set new timber against the tunnel walls.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在巷道两壁架上新的木支架。
senses.why: Underground, the same beam sense becomes a safety structure holding back falling ground.
senses.whyCN: 在地下，同样的横梁义变成了挡住塌方的安全结构。

senses.title: Personal qualities
senses.definition: used figuratively for the qualities from which a person is made
senses.definitionCN: 比喻人的素质、禀性
senses.example: The coach saw good timber in the young player.
senses.exampleCN: 教练看出这个年轻球员是块好料。
senses.why: To build something well you need good timber, so a person worth building is said to be good timber.
senses.whyCN: 要做好东西就得用好木材，于是值得造就的人也被说成好木材。

senses.title: Land covered with trees
senses.definition: forest land, especially in a phrase such as timber land
senses.definitionCN: 森林用地，尤见于 timber land 等短语
senses.example: The family owns a few acres of timber land.
senses.exampleCN: 这家拥有几英亩林地。
senses.why: Land that grows the material takes on the name of the material it produces.
senses.whyCN: 生长这种材料的土地被冠上了它所产材料的名字。

senses.title: The call that a tree is falling
senses.definition: the warning shout given when a felled tree is about to fall
senses.definitionCN: 伐倒的树将要倒下时发出的警告呼喊
senses.example: Timber went up from the far end of the clearing.
senses.exampleCN: 林间空地另一头传来「倒树了」的喊声。
senses.why: The warning names the material as it comes down, so the word becomes the shout itself.
senses.whyCN: 这声警告喊的正是落下的材料，于是词本身成了呼喊。

senses.title: A heavy usable frame
senses.definition: used for a strong person or structure that supports others
senses.definitionCN: 喻指能支撑他人的强壮的人或结构
senses.example: He was a timber of the party, steady through every crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 他是党内的一根栋梁，每次危机中都稳得住。
senses.why: A beam holds up a roof, so a person who holds up a group is compared to that beam.
senses.whyCN: 横梁撑起屋顶，撑起团体的人便被比作横梁。

intro.en: The word appears in Old English as timber, first naming a building, and Old Norse timberr carries the same senses of building and building material.
intro.cn: 这个词在古英语中作 timber，最初指建筑物；古诺斯语 timberr 同样兼有「建筑物」与「建材」两义。

items.en: Timber named a building, a structure that gives shelter.
items.cn: timber 指建筑物，即提供遮蔽的构造物。

items.en: Timberr also meant building material and influenced the northern forms.
items.cn: timberr 也指建筑材料，影响了北方各方言的形式。

items.en: The sense of wood prepared for building becomes dominant.
items.cn: 「备好的建筑用木材」这一义项成为主导。

items.en: The word extends to beams and to standing trees grown for timber.
items.cn: 本词扩展到横梁以及专为木材而种的树木。

items.en: Mining and shipbuilding give the word fixed technical senses as a support.
items.cn: 采矿与造船给本词固定的技术义：「支撑木」。

items.en: The figurative good timber and the lumberjack shout are both in common use.
items.cn: 比喻义的「好料」与伐木工的呼喊现都通用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words for pieces of wood, and the near-meaning group collects the building and forest vocabulary around this one.
note.cn: 形近组收集各类木料的词，近义组则聚集与木材相近的建筑与森林词汇。

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the building sense behind the word, its compounds, and the beams it names.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从词中的「建筑物」古义、复合词与横梁义入手。

normal.en: Timber once meant a building, so the word still carries structure inside it.
normal.cn: timber 曾指建筑物，词里仍藏着「结构」。

normal.en: Timberyard and timber frame are the two compounds easiest to hold.
normal.cn: timberyard 与 timber frame 是最容易记住的两个复合词。

normal.en: Lumber is the American cousin; timber is the standing tree or the seasoned beam.
normal.cn: lumber 是美式近亲，timber 更偏向待伐的树或备好的梁。

normal.en: Good timber is a compliment, meaning a person worth building.
normal.cn: good timber 是褒义，指值得造就的人。

normal.en: The lumberjack shout Timber uses the word itself as the warning.
normal.cn: 伐木工的喊声 Timber 就是把词本身当作警告。

abstract.en: Picture a sawn face of pine with rings running in tight curves.
abstract.cn: 想象锯开的松木截面，年轮卷成紧密的圈。

abstract.en: Think of a roof held up by dark beams crossing the ceiling.
abstract.cn: 想一根根深色横梁在天花板上交错的屋顶。

abstract.en: A forest is a warehouse of timber standing on its own roots.
abstract.cn: 森林就是一座长在根上的木料仓库。

examples.en: The house uses timber from the nearby forest.
examples.cn: 这幢房子用的是附近森林的木材。

examples.en: Two roof timbers were replaced after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后更换了两根屋顶横梁。

examples.en: The scouts learned to shout timber before a tree fell.
examples.cn: 童子军学会在树倒下前喊「倒树了」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提木伯」——那位伯伯一提木头就懂，木料好坏一看便知。

root: 古英语 timber（建筑物）受古诺斯语 timberr（建筑、建材）影响，义转为「建筑用木材」，再引申为横梁、林木与「人的素质」。

sensesIntro.en: Starting from a built structure, the entry moves through the wood it is made of, the beams and mine props, the forest that supplies it, and the human qualities that building needs.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词从「建成的构造」出发，经过所用的木料、横梁与矿用支架、供材的森林，走到建造所需的人的素质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: squared beams stacked and waiting to become a structure.
core.cn: 核心意象：码放整齐的木方，等着被搭成构造。

branches.en: Prepared wood and the land that produces it.
branches.cn: 备好的木料与出产木料的土地。

branches.en: Trees regarded as a harvest.
branches.cn: 作为收成的树木。

branches.en: Structural and supporting wood.
branches.cn: 结构与支撑用的木料。

branches.en: The beam as a metaphor for support.
branches.cn: 横梁作为支撑的比喻。

branches.en: Human quality and the warning shout.
branches.cn: 人的素质与倒树的警告喊声。

intro.en: The noun is native and takes the ordinary English endings for its adjective and noun forms, plus compounds with yard and frame.
intro.cn: 这是个本土名词，加常规英语词尾构成形容词与名词形式，并与 yard、frame 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the Latin lines below list borrowed words for wood and for building that often pair with timber in technical texts.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；下面列出的拉丁词是技术文献中常与 timber 搭配的借词。

items.exampleCN: 全词意义都落在这个名词上。

items.example: It reinforced the material sense in northern English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英格兰北方强化了「材料」义。

items.example: Timbering names the wooden supports of a shaft.
items.exampleCN: timbering 指矿井巷道的木支撑。

items.meaning: an enclosed place for work or storage
items.meaningCN: 用于作业或存放的场地
items.example: Timberyard is where boards are stacked.
Timber frame is a kind of construction.
items.exampleCN: timber frame 是一种结构方式。

items.meaning: a structure built of a material
items.example: Timberwork appears on old house fronts.
items.exampleCN: timberwork 出现在老房子的正立面上。
